name: Systematic OTM Tail-Hedge Put
summary: Systematically buy small amounts of far-OTM index puts every month as a convexity sleeve. Loses small amounts continuously and pays enormously in a crash.
max_profit: Very large multiples (10x-50x) in a >15% drawdown event
max_loss: The full monthly debit, which is the expected outcome in roughly 11 of 12 months
breakevens: strike - debit; far below spot, so it only pays in genuine tails

greeks.gamma: tiny at rest, explosive in a selloff
greeks.theta: negative, small in dollars but 100% of the position decays most months
greeks.vega: positive; far-OTM puts carry the steepest skew and gain the most vega in a panic

typical_dte: 45-90 DTE, rolled monthly to maintain a ladder
when_to_use: As a permanent, small, budgeted sleeve rather than a timed trade. Do not try to time it - the cost of missing the one month that pays exceeds the savings.
entry_rules: Fixed monthly budget: 0.15% of equity per month (~$75 on $50k), capped at 1.8%/yr
Buy on a fixed calendar day (e.g. the first trading day of each month) - no discretion, no timing
Delta -0.03 to -0.07 on SPY or QQQ, 45-90 DTE
Skip the month only if VIX > 30 at the scheduled buy (skew is then prohibitively expensive)
Log separately from directional P&L so the sleeve's drag is visible and intentional
management_rules: Do nothing in normal months - let them decay
Monetisation ladder: sell 25% of the sleeve at 5x the debit, another 25% at 10x, another 25% at 20x, hold the last 25% to the exit rule
Roll the ladder monthly; do not let the sleeve go empty
Never increase the budget after a scare
exit_rules: Positions are held until the monetisation ladder triggers or until 7 DTE, at which point any remaining value is sold and the contract abandoned if worthless
Any contract still ITM must be closed by 15:30 ET on expiration day to avoid auto-exercise into short index shares
assignment_risk: None (long). Auto-exercise into short SPY is the only operational hazard.
liquidity_needs: SPY/QQQ only; far-OTM puts there still carry OI in the thousands.
common_mistakes: Abandoning the sleeve after a year of losses right before it would have paid; scaling it up after a small scare.
